dataset: synthetic cross-industry campaigns; no real ByteDance or Tencent results
evaluation: The gate grew from 29 to 33 checks as manual review exposed path, cohort and metric-lineage failures. Counts below preserve the gate version used at each run.
claim_boundary: Paired development cases, not a pass-rate estimate or proof of business decision quality.

runs.initial_evaluator_result: 28/29: diagnosis_matches_task falsely failed because the checker ignored the user's explicit channel request in the same turn
runs.manual_review: The variant and channel drill-downs were relevant; channel cost was correctly identified as not allocatable, so no channel-level efficiency was claimed.
runs.disposition: The evaluator now considers both structured task context and explicit user text; the prior restrictive rule remains when no channel need is stated.

runs.manual_review: The model twice supplied a modified scope to diagnose_dimension. Both calls were rejected; the third call succeeded after reverting to the confirmed scope.
runs.disposition: The diagnosis tool no longer accepts scope as model input. It binds the server-confirmed scope internally. The failed run is retained as the regression case, not counted as a pass.

runs.manual_review: The single variant diagnosis used the server-confirmed scope, answered the task-path question and cited its own evidence. No scope correction call occurred.
Both drill-downs used the bound scope. The answer kept cost allocation and causal boundaries explicit.

runs.current_result: failed after the experiment-control-cohort gate was added
runs.manual_review: The path-stage interpretation was fixed, but the action randomized only the existing stage-task cohort while naming the historical login-gift cohort as the experiment control.
runs.disposition: Added a hard gate requiring new and unchanged experiences to be randomized inside the same eligible cohort; historical variants may only be observational references.

runs.current_result: failed 31/33 after arithmetic and statistical-lineage gates were added
runs.manual_review: The control cohort was fixed, but one sentence paired activation-to-path-purchase rates (19.41% and 9.71%) with the 4.81pp confidence interval and p-value computed for purchase-per-exposure.
runs.disposition: The tool now labels its inferential metric explicitly; gates check nearby rate arithmetic and prevent path-stage rates from borrowing purchase-per-exposure statistics.

runs.manual_review: Path-stage rates are descriptive and separated from the purchase-per-exposure confidence interval and p-value. The proposed control is inside the same eligible stage-task cohort; the login-gift variant is only an observational reference.
runs.claim_boundary: One passing synthetic run after two newly discovered semantic failures is regression evidence, not a reliability rate.
